text:
incidents-bot: PAGING: streaming-service p99 latency SLO breach in pool-gpu-mt-3 — alert A-2026-5077. p95=420ms (baseline 120ms), p99=8.2s (baseline 400ms). Streaming stalls reported. Auto-escalating to on-call.

alex (on-call): on it. looking at console now. linking dashboard: https://console.redwood/alerts/A-2026-5077 

Maya SRE: grabbing tracing. seeing heavy write IO on /dev/nvme0n1 on hosts in pool-gpu-mt-3, plus cgroup throttling spikes. p99 tail correlates with iowait bursts.

Luis Infra: confirmed. iostat from host-gpu-17 shows write_qdepth jumps and avg_lat > 20ms. suspect noisy tenant causing background checkpointing.

alex (on-call): which tenant(s)? any customer-facing impact known?

Maya SRE: initial query: tenant ids T-84 and T-129 have huge KV cache evictions and sustained writeback. T-84 sessions show streaming stalls at the same timestamps.

Ash Support: i've received two customer reports of degraded streaming from acme-inc and beamapp around 15:12-15:20. they saw stalls and retries. collecting more details.

Jen Runtime: are these tenants on shared pool-gpu-mt-3? if so we can try live-mitigations: 1) throttle background IO for noisy tenant via cgroup, 2) migrate tenant to isolated pool, or 3) temporary eviction to burst queue.

alex (on-call): prefer minimal blast radius. try cgroup throttle first, then migrate if not effective. Maya, can you apply throttle? include exact commands so infra team can audit.

Maya SRE: applying soft io limit to T-84 now. command:```sudo cgset -r blkio.throttle.read_iops_device=\"8:0 1000\" -r blkio.throttle.write_iops_device=\"8:0 500\" /cgroups/tenants/T-84``` will reduce write IOPS to 500. executing.

Luis Infra: heads-up: live throttle may increase latency for T-84 but should reduce global tail. ready to cut migration if needed.

incidents-bot: config-change recorded: throttle applied to T-84 by Maya SRE at 2026-03-15T15:18:12Z.

Maya SRE: immediate effect visible — host iowait dropped ~60% on gpu-17, p99 for streaming-service reduced from 8.2s to ~1.1s in 30s. p95 back to ~170ms.

Ash Support: reporting back to acme-inc: \"we see improvements, any further issues?\" they say sessions are recovering. :thumbsup:

Jen Runtime: good. we should still evacuate noisy tenant from shared pool as follow-up — throttling is temporary mitigation.

alex (on-call): agree. start migration plan for T-84 -> dedicated-isolated-2. schedule shows capacity available. Luis can you kick off a live migration with minimal disruption?

Luis Infra: starting migration job: `./migrate-tenant --tenant T-84 --dest dedicated-isolated-2 --live` . will monitor chunk-by-chunk. ETA ~6 mins to finish, will stream progress here.

incidents-bot: migration job started job-id J-8801 by Luis Infra at 2026-03-15T15:22:03Z.

Maya SRE: continuing to watch metrics. minor spikes during chunk transfer but within SLOs. no new p99 regressions.

Luis Infra: migration complete. final handoff: T-84 now on dedicated-isolated-2, traffic cutover at 15:28:07Z. job J-8801 closed.

alex (on-call): excellent. confirm post-cut p99 for host pool-gpu-mt-3 stable at ~480ms. we can remove throttle after verifying overnight.

Maya SRE: will keep throttle for 30m and monitor ingestion and streaming dashboards. planning to remove at ~15:58 unless regressions.

Priya Product: any customer-impacting SLAs breached? need to notify affected accounts and timeline for RCA.

alex (on-call): short-term: customers saw stalls up to ~20s between 15:12-15:18 but resolved after throttle/migration. mark as partial degradation. assign follow-up RCA to SRE + Infra + Runtime.

Ash Support: I have ACME and BeamApp ticket updates queued. will include timeline and mitigation steps.

Maya SRE: immediate TODOs: 1) collect blkio histograms for T-84 and T-129, 2) run heap/kv-cache audit on T-84 workload, 3) validate autosnapshot/checkpoint schedules for noisy background jobs, 4) drop throttle after cool-down window and confirm.

Luis Infra: infra TODO: add automated noisy-tenant detection rule based on sustained writeback + cgroup throttle events, and a runbook entry for live migration steps.

alex (on-call): i'll handoff to Maya for postmortem writeup. leaving incident as acknowledged and mitigated. 

Maya SRE: taking postmortem. tagging: #postmortem-drafts and will create ticket PM-2026-88. 

incidents-bot: incident status updated to MITIGATED at 2026-03-15T15:30:25Z.

alex (on-call): thanks all. if anything reappears ping @on-call immediately. :eyes:
